In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in mega-cities with high levels of outdoor air pollution, the use of a high efficiency filter (MERV11 or greater) in combination with a reduced ventilation flow rate can provide the greatest benefit to indoor air quality.
for the case of outdoor PM2. 5, a two-filter system with high-efficiency filters (MERV 11 or higher) and low outdoor ventilation rates can be used to mitigate indoor exposure to outdoor PM2.5.

for PM2.5 removal from outdoor air, two-filter systems are more resilient than single-filter systems, especially for high ventilation rates, while for ozone removal, single-filter systems are more effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the indoor air quality of office buildings in mega cities is affected by both outdoor air pollution and building systems.
the use of high efficiency filters is not always the optimal solution for improving indoor air quality.
the building systems, including HVAC, filtration, and ventilation, can play a critical role for mitigating indoor air quality (IAQ) problems in polluted cities, especially for PM2.5.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for office buildings in polluted cities, the most effective approach for mitigating indoor PM2.5 concentrations is to use a high efficiency filter and reduce the outdoor air ventilation rate.

for office buildings in polluted cities, the use of high-efficiency filters and high outdoor ventilation rates is a more effective strategy for reducing indoor PM2.5 levels than the use of outdoor filters.
in polluted mega-cities, the use of air handling units with two filters (AHU filter and outdoor air filters) and high outdoor ventilation rates can significantly reduce indoor PM2.5 concentrations.
